Theme

Church life

bow verb

in worship

also bow down, make a bow, prostrate oneself, prostration, metania

late Latin

Vulg. Gen. 24.26

sē inclīnāre

bow (the body, before God)

Classically inclīnāre is to bend or lower; with sē, of a bow in worship, it is the Vulgate’s (Inclīnāvit sē homō, et adōrāvit Dominum). To bow the head is caput inclīnāre. In the Orthodox churches the bow from the waist with the sign of the cross (Greek μετάνοια) and the full prostration to the ground are regular parts of prayer; in the Latin rite the bow of the head or body and the genuflection are the usual signs.

Other words

  • adōrō, adōrāre, adōrāvī, adōrātum — worship, do reverence (with a bow or prostration)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Ov. Met. 3.18: Phoebum taciturnus adōrat (Lewis & Short); Suet. Vit. 2 (Lewis & Short); Vulg. Mt. 2.11

    Worship shown in a gesture, Greek προσκυνεῖν: in Rome a hand to the lips and a turn of the whole body, under the emperors a prostration (prōcumbēns, Suet. Vit. 2; Lewis & Short).

  • prōcumbō, prōcumbere, prōcubuī, prōcubitum — bow down to the ground, prostrate oneself

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. BG 7.15: prōcumbunt Gallīs omnibus ad pedēs Biturigēs (Lewis & Short)

    The full prostration: to fall forward to the ground, as suppliants did.

Examples

  • Inclīnāvit sē homō, et adōrāvit Dominum

    The man bowed and worshipped the LordVulg. Gen. 24.26

  • et prōcidentēs adōrāvērunt eum

    and they fell down and worshipped him (the Magi)Vulg. Mt. 2.11

See also bow one’s head, kneel, sign, pray.
